intro: A distribution can shift even when its mean stays fixed. The two-sample KS distance finds the largest vertical gap between empirical cumulative distributions.
task: Find the largest empirical CDF gap and its earliest location, including tied observations and unequal sample counts.
requirements: reference and current are nonempty finite numeric vectors; ties and unequal sample sizes are allowed.
Evaluate both empirical CDFs at every distinct observed value using count(sample<=value)/sample_size. Return dict statistic and location.
location is the smallest observed value attaining the maximum absolute CDF gap. Return statistic 0 and the smallest pooled observation for identical empirical distributions. No p-value is requested.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use right-sided counts
hints.body: At an observed value, include every tied observation in its empirical CDF.

hints.title: Inspect pooled support
hints.body: The CDF gap changes only at values observed in at least one sample.

explanation: The empirical CDF is a step function, so a maximum gap occurs on the pooled support. Right-sided counts handle ties as one jump rather than arbitrarily ordering equal observations.
This lesson computes a descriptive distance only. Statistical significance requires additional assumptions and a p-value procedure; those are deliberately separate from the distance.
